title: Claude Ship: What Anthropic Has Announced So Far
summary: Claude Ship launched with new capabilities for automators. Understand what changes affect your workflows and what new features become available.
body_markdown:
## Why Claude Ship matters for automation


If the launch matters, it matters only as far as it changes which tasks a team can hand to AI inside workflows it already runs. The maker's pages are the only place that change is stated.


### Where it touches an AI-plus-apps workflow


When a workflow links an AI model to business apps, it has handoff points: a record arrives, something reads it, something decides, something writes back. Claude Ship is relevant at those points and nowhere else in the argument here.


If a capability on the maker's pages doesn't alter one of those handoffs, it doesn't change an automation team's week, however good it sounds in a launch post.


### Tasks Claude Ship can now automate in workflows


Read each stated capability as a clause in an agreement, and ask what it obliges the AI to do without a person stepping in.


A capability earns a place in a workflow only when it names a task, the task sits at a handoff, and the maker's own page says so.


Anything a team infers beyond that wording is an assumption, and assumptions are what break at the first failed run.


> A capability earns a place in a workflow only when it names a task, the task sits at a handoff, and the maker's own page says so.


### What Claude Ship doesn't change in your apps


Nothing in a new release rewrites what an existing app allows. The apps keep their own permissions, their own record structures and their own failure behavior.


The review step a team put in front of a risky action still belongs there until the maker's pages say otherwise. So the first test of any handoff is still a single run against real data, with someone watching the result.
